QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Landscape and Types_5

question.text: The analyst at Kaveri Capital AIF is preparing an LP presentation. He needs to define the 'real risk-free rate' exactly as the chapter does. Which description is correct?

answer.text: The return on a one-year T-Bill after deducting the AIF's management fee.
The basic rate of return assuming no inflation and no uncertainty about future cash flows — compensation paid for postponing consumption.
The return on a listed government bond after adjusting for credit-default spread.
Nominal risk-free rate plus risk premium.

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter defines real risk-free rate as 'the basic rate of return or interest rate, assuming no inflation and no uncertainty about future cash flows — compensation paid for postponing consumption.' It is the pure time value of money. Real risk-free rate adjusted for inflation = nominal risk-free rate; adding risk premium produces the required rate of return. The Trap: (A) confuses T-Bill yield (which already contains inflation) with real rate; fees are irrelevant to definition. (C) is a credit-adjusted nominal, still not 'real'. (D) Nominal + risk premium = required rate of return, not real risk-free rate.
